levers.change: spacer mesh 380 -> 230 g/m2 on the back panel BP-01, crown pad face BP-03 and J-strap faces HS-J2
levers.strength: no load path (body-contact face); no HA-LS-1 row or bag load point touches it
levers.durability: thinner (3.0 vs 4.5 mm) face: less air gap, faster wear where the pack rubs. The record's own note says the mesh abrades in 1-2 seasons at the hip, so the hip faces are left out (N2)
levers.test: MESH-1 Martindale (ASTM D4966) both meshes to 20 000 rev + MESH-2 3-tester 2 h sweat carry at 30 kg (BP-3 back-pressure strips under the rails); fallback today's mesh
levers.look: none visible from outside (wearer face); finer texture on the back panel
records: spacer_mesh_3d_230 (3 mm, 230 g/m2): gsm, thickness, compression, abrasion, roll width, price

levers.change: belt wing and lumbar mesh faces 380 -> 320 g/m2 (hip faces keep a dense mesh)
levers.durability: 320 g/m2 is a 3 mm inelastic mesh sold for backpacks; hip abrasion is the risk
levers.test: MESH-1 (same lot) + HB-1 hipbelt pressure / hold with the 3 mm face; fallback today's mesh
records: spacer_mesh_3d_320 (3 mm inelastic): gsm (listing 320 vs page title 390), abrasion, roll width

levers.change: US1/US2 tri-glide backstops stainless 11 g -> titanium 4 g (2)
levers.strength: the US rows are governed by the 25 mm cam (1100 N slip, margin 1.53 on 720 N) and the box-X (4.43); the backstop is not credited in any SF row. It must still stop a slipping cam: same US-BS gate as the stainless part. Ti-6Al-4V (record) is stronger than 304 per section
levers.durability: titanium does not corrode; webbing wear on a thinner bar edge unknown
levers.test: US-BS run on the Ti tri-glide (cam slipped to the backstop, 1080 N hold, dry / wet / -20 C, 5 samples) + weigh 5; fallback stainless
records: triglide_25mm_ti: mass (4 g secondary), bar section, rated hold

levers.change: frame-side roll-top collar B-06f ULTRA 200X -> 70D ripstop (the aft collar B-06 is already 70D)
levers.strength: no load point: the roll-top clips RT / RTM sit on the hem B-07 and the gusset B-03, not on B-06f
levers.durability: B-06f rides against the crown top bar and the B-25 bridle when rolled: 70D (Martindale >10 000) against ULTRA's Taber 4400 is a real abrasion step down
levers.test: AB-2 crown-bar rub: a rolled 70D collar on a bar offcut with the bridle, 5 000 cycles of the pack's pitch swing, no hole; fallback ULTRA 200X
levers.look: better: 70D comes in the solid house colours (ULTRA has few colours, record ir_notes)

levers.change: rail sleeves BP-05 (pair) and crown pad back BP-07: Robic 210D -> 70D ripstop
levers.strength: no rated load: the sleeve holds the rail foam and the carbon backer on the stay line
levers.durability: the sleeve back sits between the backer strip and the stay; carbon-edge chafe on 70D is the risk
levers.test: SLV-1: sleeve on the backer strip edge, 10 000 rub cycles at the rev C skin pressure, no wear-through; fallback 210D

levers.change: haul-wrap webbing W1-W3 (cut for carry) polyester 18 g/m -> thin Dyneema 25 mm 10.2 g/m
levers.strength: webbing break 11768 N vs 225 N factored (S9): x52; box-X 3186 N is the thread path (unchanged); the governing part is the heavy ladder lock slip (490 N ASSUMPTION on polyester): unknown on 0.7 mm UHMWPE, which the maker says suits buckles only in limited use. Gate before booking
levers.durability: UHMWPE creeps under constant load and is slick in a ladder lock; it twists; cuts need a hot knife
levers.test: LL-D: 5 heavy ladder locks on the Dyneema webbing, 338 N proof (W-PULL) dry / wet / -20 C, slip < 5 mm; W-box pull to 338 N on a 0.7 mm specimen; fallback polyester
levers.look: black only (Dyneema dyes poorly); thinner, slightly sheened straps on the outside of the bag
records: dyneema_webbing_25mm_thin: g/m, break, ladder-lock slip (Extremtextil art. 72979)
levers.source: corrie_f W-web / A-2 / BL-031 rows / 18 g/m x (10.2 - 18) g/m; research 3.3

levers.change: J-strap shells HS-J1 and belt wing / lumbar shells: 330D CORDURA -> ULTRAGrid 210D (the bag-body cloth)
levers.strength: the strap and belt shells carry part of the strap and wing tension; ULTRAGrid's grab (1300 / 1100 N) is above 330D's (1000 / 800 N), but both are record ESTIMATEs / ASSUMPTIONs, so a seam pull decides
levers.durability: Taber 1100 vs 330D 800 (records): level or better; UHMWPE grid yarns need tighter SPI and bartacks
levers.test: SH-1 strap-to-yoke and wing-root seam pulls on ULTRAGrid (1.5 x the HS-1 strap load), plus the owner swatch already gated for the bag body (A_fab); fallback 330D
levers.look: grid lines visible on straps and belt; matches the bag body (one cloth language)
levers.source: build_geometry HS-J1 + ledger belt shell rows x (1 - 132/180); records
